```markdown
# sec-filing-ingestion — Roadmap

## Outcomes

Source: your partner's words, 2026-11-06. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md, specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`).
uv workspace of four packages: sec-edgar-client, sec-edgar-download, sec-edgar-index-ingest, sec-edgar-ingest (root `pyproject.toml`).

| # | Outcome | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | The quarterly and daily index files, ingested into one filing-index table | A | 1 | Small: about 130 quarterly files since 1993 plus one daily file per business day, minutes of downloading at 3 requests/second (SEC full-index and daily-index directories); measured by Stage 1 |
| O2 | The individual submissions that the index rows name, downloaded | A | 2 | Large: millions of files, weeks for the full history at 3 requests/second (index row count × request rate); one quarter measured by Stage 2 |
| O3 | 10-K and 8-K filings handled: picked out of the submissions, with their main documents extracted | A | 3 | Unknown until submissions are on disk; measured by Stage 3 |

Tracks: A — SEC filing ingestion (known progression).

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Filing-index table
      Objective: Load the real quarterly and daily index files into one filing-index table.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: nothing (package scaffolds only)
      Produces: a filing-index table queryable by CIK, form type, filing date and archive path; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1 — the table holds rows from every real quarterly index in the chosen range plus the open quarter's daily indexes; findings record files fetched, bytes, rows, elapsed time and observed request rate of the real run
      Leaves out: manifest, provenance, replay from raw snapshots, reconciliation and index validation suite (Stage 4); shared request budget and resume (Stage 5); scheduling and deployment (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Submissions for one quarter
      Objective: Download the submissions that one real quarter's index rows name.
      Outcomes: O2 (one quarter)
      Consumes: Stage 1 filing-index table
      Produces: one quarter of submissions on disk, addressable from their index rows; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-2-findings.md
      Exit: O2 — every submission named by the chosen quarter's index rows is on disk or listed as failed; findings record file count, bytes, elapsed time, request rate and the extrapolated full-history cost
      Leaves out: shared request budget and resume (Stage 5); full-history download and submission manifest (Stage 6); scheduling and deployment (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 3: 10-K and 8-K for one quarter
      Objective: Pick the 10-K and 8-K filings out of Stage 2's quarter and extract their main documents.
      Outcomes: O3 (one quarter)
      Consumes: Stage 2 submissions on disk
      Produces: extracted 10-K and 8-K main documents for one quarter; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-3-findings.md
      Exit: O3 — every 10-K and 8-K in the quarter has an extracted main document or a recorded failure reason; findings record counts, extraction failures, elapsed time and the extrapolated full-history cost
      Leaves out: filing validation suite across historical formats and filing provenance (Stage 7); scheduling and deployment (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: Index catalog hardening
      Objective: Bring the filing-index table up to a durable catalog standard.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: Stage 1 filing-index table and findings
      Produces: manifest, provenance, replay from raw snapshots, reconciliation and index validation suite for the filing index
      Exit: O1 — a parser change rebuilds the table from stored raw index files with no SEC requests; a changed quarterly file is reconciled with its changes recorded; the index validation suite passes over the formats in the chosen range
      Leaves out: shared request budget and resume (Stage 5); scheduling and deployment (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 5: Shared SEC access
      Objective: Route all SEC requests, index and submission alike, through one request budget with resumable work units.
      Outcomes: O1, O2
      Consumes: Stage 2 downloader; Stage 4 manifest
      Produces: shared request budget and resume for every SEC-facing command
      Exit: O1, O2 — concurrent index and submission runs never exceed the configured request rate in total; an interrupted run resumes without re-downloading completed files
      Leaves out: scheduling and deployment (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 6: Submissions full history
      Objective: Download the submissions for the whole indexed range.
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: Stage 2 findings (measured cost); Stage 5 shared request budget and resume
      Produces: full-history submissions on disk with a submission manifest
      Exit: O2 — every submission named by the filing-index table is on disk or listed in the submission manifest as failed or pending, with no silent gaps; the campaign's elapsed time and request rate are recorded
      Leaves out: scheduling and deployment (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 7: 10-K and 8-K across history
      Objective: Extend 10-K and 8-K handling to every quarter on disk.
      Outcomes: O3
      Consumes: Stage 3 findings; Stage 6 full-history submissions
      Produces: filing validation suite across historical formats and filing provenance; extracted main documents for the full range
      Exit: O3 — every 10-K and 8-K in the range has an extracted main document traceable to its submission, or a recorded failure; the filing validation suite passes over the historical formats found
      Leaves out: scheduling and deployment (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 8: Scheduling and deployment
      Objective: Run daily index ingestion, reconciliation, submission catch-up and 10-K/8-K handling as scheduled operations on a deployed platform.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3
      Consumes: Stages 4–7
      Produces: scheduling and deployment for every pipeline
      Exit: O1, O2, O3 — observed scheduled runs (not manual runs) ingest new daily indexes, download their submissions and extract new 10-K and 8-K documents, each with a durable run report
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: brainstorming

## Stage-spec stamp

Every stage spec's Rollout note carries this line, which writing-plans copies verbatim into the stage plan's header:

> Roadmap: specs/sec-filing-ingestion-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

When every stage is ticked, run derive-roadmap §6 over the Outcomes list (O1–O3): one verdict per outcome with evidence (implementing stage and plan, Deviation notes, deferred_items entries). Each unmet outcome becomes a new stage or a written deferral.
```

---

Do you approve this 8-stage partition? The order follows your ranking (O1 → O2 → O3, each on real data first), with the hardening stages after. On a yes, I'll commit `specs/sec-filing-ingestion-roadmap.md` on `main` and hand off Stage 1.
